story.title: Eric Bauza, Renowned Voice Actor of Looney Tunes Characters, Passes Away at 46
story.summary: Eric Bauza, the Emmy-winning voice actor known for voicing iconic Looney Tunes characters such as Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, has died at the age of 46. His family confirmed his passing, which occurred on Sunday. Bauza's career included roles in various animated series and films, contributing significantly to the legacy of beloved characters.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about Bauza’s death?
explore_lenses.title: Family confirmation and a medical finding
explore_lenses.summary: Bauza’s family described his death as sudden; subsequent reporting cited the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner’s determination of hypertensive cardiovascular disease. The public record establishes a medical cause, but not a fuller account of the circumstances.

claims.text: Bauza’s family said he died suddenly late Sunday, October 25, 2026.
The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner reported hypertensive cardiovascular disease as the cause of death, according to AP’s link to the county case record.
Bauza’s manager, Judy Coppage, called the death a sudden shock and said it was a profound loss for his family, the animation industry and fans.

explore_lenses.label: Why was Bauza important to Looney Tunes?
explore_lenses.title: A custodian of characters across generations
explore_lenses.summary: Bauza was not simply associated with one cartoon role: he performed several central Looney Tunes characters while explicitly treating Mel Blanc’s work as the foundation. His death therefore removes a performer who helped carry a long-running franchise into contemporary film and television.

claims.text: Bauza voiced Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Porky Pig and other Looney Tunes characters, including Elmer Fudd, Marvin the Martian, Foghorn Leghorn, Tweety and the Road Runner.
In a 2026 interview, Bauza said his work was based on original Looney Tunes voice actor Mel Blanc, whom he called the blueprint for the characters.
Bauza told the Associated Press that Looney Tunes’ voices and visual style had influenced him as an artist, and AP reported that he approached Blanc’s performances reverentially.
AP reported that he accumulated more than 400 voice-acting credits beginning in 2001 and won three Children’s and Family Emmy Awards between 2022 and 2025.

explore_lenses.label: What projects and roles may be affected?
explore_lenses.title: No successor or production plan announced
explore_lenses.summary: Bauza remained publicly active shortly before his death, including on the 2026 Looney Tunes film “Coyote vs. Acme.” But the reviewed reporting does not identify a replacement performer or any official plan for his continuing characters.

claims.text: AP photographed Bauza promoting “Coyote vs. Acme” in June 2026 and attending its Los Angeles premiere on August 26, 2026.
CBS reported that Bauza discussed “Coyote vs. Acme” and the newest Looney Tunes installment in an August 2026 interview.
No named studio, producer or rights holder in the reviewed sources had announced who, if anyone, would take over Bauza’s Looney Tunes roles.

story_report.summary: Eric Bauza, the Emmy-winning voice actor who became a leading modern interpreter of Looney Tunes characters including Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Porky Pig, has died at 46, his family confirmed. The family said he died suddenly late Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026; the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner listed hypertensive cardiovascular disease as the cause of death. His death leaves no publicly announced plan for who, if anyone, will assume his Looney Tunes roles.

sections.heading: Bauza’s Looney Tunes Legacy
sections.body: Bauza voiced a broad roster of Looney Tunes characters beyond Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Porky Pig, including Elmer Fudd, Marvin the Martian, Foghorn Leghorn, Tweety and the Road Runner. He said original performer Mel Blanc was the blueprint for the characters, and told the Associated Press that the franchise’s voices and visual style had influenced him as an artist. AP reported that Bauza earned more than 400 voice-acting credits after beginning in 2001 and won three Children’s and Family Emmy Awards from 2022 through 2025.

sections.heading: Bauza Remained Active in 2026
sections.body: Bauza was still promoting Looney Tunes work in the months before his death. AP photographed him promoting “Coyote vs. Acme” in June 2026 and attending its Los Angeles premiere on Aug. 26, while CBS reported that he discussed the film and the newest Looney Tunes installment in an August interview. His manager, Judy Coppage, described the death as a sudden shock and a profound loss for his family, the animation industry and fans.

unresolved.text: The reporting reviewed does not provide a fuller public account of the circumstances of Bauza’s death or any memorial plans.
No studio, producer or rights holder had publicly announced whether Bauza’s roles would be recast, whether completed recordings would be used, or how future Looney Tunes productions might change.

related_stories.title: Microsoft Proposes Buyouts to 60,000 Employees Amid Cost-Cutting Efforts
related_stories.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to approximately 60,000 employees, which represents about a quarter of its workforce. This initiative is part of the company's strategy to reduce costs while increasing investments in artificial intelligence. The buyout offers will be available to staff globally, including those in the UK.

related_stories.title: Sudan Faces Widespread Power Outages Following RSF Drone Attacks
related_stories.summary: Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) conducted a coordinated drone strike on five power stations, leading to significant power outages across the eastern regions of the country. The attacks targeted two power stations each in Al-Jazira and Gedaref states, and one in White Nile state, affecting large areas of these regions, according to a government official.
